setting: You both live in Leeds, England, in the same city but not the same house. Pauline is Hannah's grandmother, and Hannah has grown up close to her, visiting most Sundays since childhood. You both know each other's routines, friends and most family news, and you have chatted here a few times before, last about whether the Leeds Christmas markets were worth the crowds.
opener: Asking Hannah whether she is still coming for Sunday lunch.

Pauline.knows: You know Hannah is your granddaughter, the older of your son's two daughters, and you have watched her grow up into a careful, busy young woman.
Pauline.like: You are warm but direct, with a dry sense of humour that Hannah has learned to read. You have firm opinions about books, gardening and anyone who lets the Yorkshire puddings go flat, and you fuss over Hannah while teasing her about her untidy kitchen.
Pauline.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when you have something to share or need a quick answer about plans.
Pauline.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, use the occasional smiley, and rarely use abbreviations.

Hannah.knows: You know Pauline is your grandmother, the one who taught you to read and still checks your coat is buttoned before you go out.
Hannah.like: You are quick-witted, a bit impatient, and easily distracted by a good project or a cheap deal online. You tease Pauline about her strong opinions and look out for her without making a fuss, though you do get a little exasperated when she insists on helping with the move.
Hannah.texts: You message in this chat now and then, usually when you need to coordinate or want to share something amusing.
Hannah.style: You type quickly in lowercase, use common abbreviations like "thx" and "rn", and sometimes add a single emoji.

private_lines.Pauline: You live in a terraced house in Headingley, Leeds, and you are a retired school librarian who still volunteers on Thursdays at the local library. This week you have a physio appointment for your knee on Wednesday, and you are planning the Sunday roast for the family.
private_lines.Hannah: You live in a rented flat in Hyde Park, Leeds, and you work as a junior architect at a firm near the station. This week you are packing up boxes because you are moving to a new flat in Chapel Allerton on Saturday, and you are juggling late site meetings.

situation: A grandmother and her grown-up granddaughter.

text: Hannah, are you still coming for Sunday lunch? I need to know how many to cook for and whether to bother with the good beef.
still coming yes. sorry was in a site meeting til gone 6. beef is a yes obviously
Good. Your dad says he'll bring the wine and I'm not to let him choose it, so I'll expect something drinkable from you.
ha ok. i'll bring a bottle that isn't from the offer table in tesco
I've had my physio letter through. Wednesday at half ten, so I'll be at the Infirmary and not the library. Can you believe they want me to bend it like a teenager on a Wednesday?
oof. do you want me to come with you wed? i'm free after 4 probably
Don't be daft, you'll be at your desk. Your Uncle Mike is driving me. He's delighted to have a reason to sit in a car park with a flask.
he's always been first in line for a flask 😂
boxes are everywhere. have you seen the tape gun anywhere at yours? i swear i left it on the bookshelf
I haven't seen it, and I'm not having you blame me for it. Check under the cookery books. You put them down there last time you were here, I'm certain of it.
found it. under the cookery books. thx
Are you still wanting me to help with the move on Saturday or have you finally decided I'm too old to lift anything?
you are not coming to lift anything. you can sit in the new flat and tell me where the kettle goes
I'll have you know I'm perfectly capable of carrying a box of tea towels.
ok ok. tea towels only. don't tell mum i let you near the boxes
I've started the stock for Sunday. The kitchen smells like a Sunday already, which is more than I can say for your flat I'm sure.
rude. my flat is fine. it's just in boxes rn
ok i'm going to say this once: please do not lift the big bookcase on saturday even if i'm not looking
sorry, is it ok if i come a bit later sunday? site thing might run over
Later is fine as long as the beef isn't. I'll keep it warm but I won't keep it forever.
Are you bringing anyone or just the wine?
just me. and the wine that isn't from tesco 😂
Good girl.
Your Uncle Mike rang. He wants to know if he's allowed to bring the sprouts or whether I've already ruined them in my head.
tell him yes he can bring sprouts. tell him not to bring the ones he did last year
I'm not telling him that, you tell him.
boxes are multiplying. someone left a flat pack in the hall. i think it's from the landlord, which is either a gift or a threat
Put it on the list for the landlord and don't build anything until you've read the instructions. Your grandad once put a shelf up upside down and we still don't talk about it.
ha. ok. no building 😂
mum says you're going to the infirmary tomorrow with mike. do you want me to get you something from the cafe after
A tea and a sausage roll if they still do them. Don't you dare bring me one of those salads with the seeds on top.
noted. no seeds
Physio have just rung to check I'm going. I said I'd been going since 1974 and they didn't laugh.
lol. did they at least say you'll be able to bend it by sunday
They said I should be able to bend it by Christmas if I do the exercises, which is a very different promise to the one I was hoping for.
ok i'm about to be eaten by a bubble wrap situation so i'll talk later. don't cook the potatoes before i get there 🙃
